scores.claim_text: Ballard signed a commercial agreement with New Flyer for 50 MW of fuel cell bus engines (Mar 10, 2026) on top of an earlier Nov 4, 2024 PO for 200 fuel cell engines.
supports: edgar_fts.query_fulltext(search_term='Ballard', cik=NFI 0001072627): 0 hits — NFI Group does not file on EDGAR (Canadian filer on SEDAR); absence is jurisdiction-driven, not contradictory.

edgar_fts.query_fulltext(search_term='New Flyer', cutoff=2026-05-16): 67 total hits across EDGAR but the top hits are Ballard's OWN 40-F MD&A from 2019 — i.e., the partnership has been touted by Ballard for ~7+ years but the only EDGAR validations are Ballard-self-references.
scores.M_value: 0 EDGAR hits in NFI; cross-filer hits dominated by Ballard's own filings.
scores.interpretation: Calibration heuristic 7 (counterparty disclosure) is weakened by source-jurisdiction mismatch — NFI Group is Canadian and not on EDGAR, so absence is not a hard contradiction. But the 50 MW figure is ANNOUNCED commercial agreement language (heuristic 3: planned-vs-operational ladder) without disclosed delivery schedule or cumulative MW-deployed reconciliation in this filing-cache slice. Combined with the longstanding 200-engine PO from Nov 2024 still being characterized in 2026 as the basis for a 'commercial agreement,' this is a textbook headline-engine-count claim without a verified shipped-fraction. Score MODERATE.

scores.claim_text: CPKC follow-on order for approximately 20 MW of Ballard fuel cell engines for North American locomotives (Dec 5, 2024).

scores.M_value: 0 hits for any term in CIK 0001770787 — the CIK is effectively absent from the fulltext index (likely a SEDAR-only filer).
scores.interpretation: Source-jurisdiction mismatch (heuristic 5): Canadian Pacific Kansas City is a Canadian filer; its disclosures live in SEDAR, not EDGAR. SUPPLEMENT: querying the legacy CP CIK 0000016875 (pre-Kansas-City-Southern-merger) showed 5 Ballard mentions in 2021 (1x 8-K + 3x 10-Q), so CP HAS historically referenced Ballard in EDGAR. Post-CPKC merger (CIK 0001770787) shows 0 Ballard mentions through cutoff — i.e. the disclosed 'follow-on order' from Dec 2024 is NOT picked up in CPKC's subsequent filings under the new CIK. Mark UNVERIFIABLE rather than RED_FLAG because the merger-driven CIK change may shift fulltext indexing patterns; nonetheless, a 20 MW locomotive engine order from a Class 1 railroad would normally be material to that railroad's hydrogen-strategy disclosure. Mid-ladder claim (PO not yet delivered) with weak corroboration.

scores.claim_text: Strategic realignment to achieve positive cash flow under new leadership (Jul 31, 2025); leadership transition (Jun 16, 2025); new COO Ralph Robinett (Apr 13, 2026).
supports: Press-release titles in 6-K cache lay out a textbook distress cascade in <12 months: June 2025 leadership transition -> June 12, 2025 fresh Base Shelf Prospectus (refresh capacity for dilution) -> July 31, 2025 'Strategic Realignment ... Achieve Positive Cash Flow Under New Leadership' (implicit admission that cash flow is negative and prior plan is failing) -> April 13, 2026 new COO -> May 14, 2026 Weichai (long-standing strategic investor) board departure and equity sale -> 2x SCHEDULE 13D/A filed 2026-05-13 and 2026-05-15.
edgar_fts.query_fulltext('Ballard Power', forms=40-F,40-F/A,6-K,SC 13D...): 26 hits — 2x SC 13G/A and 2x SC 13D/A clustered around the Weichai exit period.

40-F cover confirms PFIC status — i.e. >75% gross income passive OR >50% assets passive. For a 'commercial' fuel-cell company this is itself a yellow-flag (cash earning passive income exceeds operating revenue, or assets are heavily held-for-investment).
scores.M_check: Distress-cascade pattern across EDGAR filing types and dates
scores.M_value: Cluster of leadership change + realignment + shelf-refresh + strategic-investor exit + 13D/A activity within 10 months.
scores.interpretation: Heuristic 10 explicitly elevates this combination. ATM-capable shelf + going-concern-adjacent 'achieve positive cash flow' language + foundational strategic investor (Weichai, an OEM customer since the 2018 JV era) exiting both board and equity = clear distress signal. PFIC classification is the bow on top. SEVERE.

scores.claim_text: Weichai's nominee directors resigned and Weichai sold its Ballard shares (May 14, 2026).
supports: edgar_fts.query_fulltext('Weichai', cik=BLDP 0001453015): 30 hits — Weichai is referenced in Ballard 40-Fs back to 2019 (Guangdong Synergy JV / Weichai-Ballard Hy-Energy etc.). I.e., Weichai has been a foundational disclosed strategic investor for 5+ years.
edgar_fts.query_fulltext('Weichai Ballard'): 39 hits.

Press-release title May 14, 2026 directly states Weichai's nominee directors RESIGNED AND Weichai SOLD its shares — i.e., a full exit two days before the cutoff. Two SCHEDULE 13D/A filings on 2026-05-13 and 2026-05-15 corroborate filing-mechanics of an exit.
scores.M_check: Ballard historical filings for Weichai relationship; SC 13D/A clustering on exit dates
scores.M_value: 5+ year disclosed relationship through 2024 -> full board+equity exit in May 2026.
scores.interpretation: Heuristic 4 (investment-vs-operating): Weichai was always equity-cross investor not firm offtake, but losing your largest long-standing strategic investor + customer simultaneously two days before our cutoff is a hard negative signal for the forward thesis. Cohort metadata explicitly lists Weichai as a long-running OEM-partnership that did not convert to scaled commercial revenue — the exit confirms the partnership has now structurally terminated. RED_FLAG_NEGATIVE on the broader 'partnership-driven commercialization' narrative.

scores.claim_text: Ballard's 2024-2026 order book is composed of many small fragmented orders (1.5 / 5 / 6 / 6.4 / 8 / 20 / 50 MW) across disparate counterparties — pattern of failed conversion to scaled hyperscaler-grade offtake.

Largest single MW figure is 50 MW (New Flyer) — equivalent in capacity terms to ~ a fraction of a single hyperscaler data-center campus. No utility / hyperscaler / heavy-industry counterparty appears.

edgar_fts.query_fulltext('Ballard fuel cell'): 36 total hits — only ONE non-Ballard counterparty filing visible (Canadian Pacific 8-K 2021-03-12). 35 of 36 are Ballard self-references. Heuristic 7 (counterparty-disclosure threshold) — no Microsoft, Amazon, Meta, Google, NextEra, Duke, Nucor, Cleveland-Cliffs, Walmart, FedEx, UPS, Toyota, Honda mentions Ballard in this aggregate set.

Cohort metadata explicitly flags 'Long history of OEM partnership announcements (Audi, Weichai, Solaris) that did not convert to scaled commercial revenue' — the 2025-2026 pattern is exactly this pattern continuing.
scores.M_check: Aggregate counterparty-disclosure threshold across all relevant hyperscaler/utility/heavy-industry CIKs implicitly via broad EDGAR + structural shape of MW order book
scores.M_value: 1 non-Ballard counterparty filing referencing Ballard fuel cell in EDGAR fulltext; 35 self-references.
scores.interpretation: Heuristic 11 / hydrogen-distress fingerprint: revenue recognition for a 50 MW commercial agreement is recognized in stages, but the structural absence of a single >100 MW offtake or any hyperscaler-grade contract, combined with the strategic-realignment / Weichai-exit / shelf-refresh distress cascade, makes the forward-revenue claims especially fragile. Score SEVERE on the structural pattern (NOT a hard RED_FLAG because individual order claims could be real-but-small).
